O.content: The title reads "Additional Promotion Weeks: Ad Spend vs Sales," and the plot shows five labeled weekly points.
No visible legend, control group, profitability measure, cost threshold, causal annotation, or full-data analysis is shown in the chart area.

B.text: If approving broader spend requires evidence that spend itself, rather than other promotion-week factors, drove sales or that the increase is financially justified, then a five-point observational scatterplot without controls, costs, margins, or causal analysis is insufficient and the appropriate action is to request full-data analysis.
B.conditions: Applies when approval requires causal, profitability, or broader-data validation; none of those requirements or results is visibly supplied.

O.content: The horizontal axis is visibly labeled "Advertising Spend ($ thousands)" and the vertical axis is visibly labeled "Sales ($ thousands)".
The blue points labeled Week 7, Week 8, Week 9, Week 10, and Week 11 progress from lower-left to upper-right on the page.
Week 7 is plotted near the x-axis tick 30 and between the y-axis ticks 60 and 70, while Week 11 is plotted near x-axis tick 70 and y-axis tick 160.

B.text: If the horizontal axis encodes advertising spend and the vertical axis encodes sales, both in $ thousands, then points farther right and higher represent weeks with greater plotted spend and greater plotted sales; if this five-week pattern is accepted as sufficient evidence for budget expansion despite no causal-validation requirement, approve broader ad spend increase.
B.conditions: Applies only if the axis labels correctly bind to the plotted points and an observed positive association is considered sufficient for approval.
